$comment: Every run of this conformance corpus by an implementation independent of the specification's author, one row per posted run. This file is the record the independence column's prose is derived from: scripts/independent-runs-gate.py computes the not-run set as the revisions from 1 to the current suiteRevision that no row here names, and fails when the prose in README.md or docs/IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT.md names a different set. A row is what licenses a figure in the prose, so do not add one for a run that was not posted with a record. Each figure is transcribed exactly as posted and names every document that carries it, so a figure cannot be quietly inflated in one of them: never rounded, never restated as a fraction of a different corpus, and never re-characterised as unprompted when their author called the run directed. Where this repository does not carry a value it records null beside a note saying so, rather than leaving the field out, because an absent field and an unrecorded fact read the same in a diff.
independence: from-spec Rust verifier with its own I-JSON parser, RFC 8785 serializer, RFC 6962 Merkle root, run-binding derivation and Ed25519 tier, built with no sight of the reference code
currentRevisionSource: vectors/CHANGES.md, the per-revision changelog that owns revision numbering. It is read rather than restated here: a revision number written in this file could only ever agree with itself.

his last author-run, and the revision his CI now verifies continuously. The suite commit the record names no longer resolves in a fresh clone of this repository, because the history it sat on was rewritten here after he pinned it; 8959bd3 carries the identical tree and therefore the identical 153 vectors, and is where a reproduction should point until the record is repinned. The unchanged revision-5 build scored 151/153 against it: ok-036 and bad-742 passed on the container-branch counter already in place, and bad-743 and bad-744 did not, because that build had not implemented the RFC 7493 section 2.1 noncharacter exclusion this revision makes normative.

runs.digestNote: the headline figure is the blind first run and no digest names the build that produced it. His reports/INDEX.json carries an explicit null digest for that record beside a sourceUnrecoverable field saying the blind build was never committed on its own -- 46ca0ee carries both the v0.7 implementation and the published number, so no tree in his repository hashes to it -- rather than borrowing the directed build's digest, which would name a different implementation. He records this as a breach of rule 6 of his own PROTOCOL-v0.7.md, the rule that run's protocol fixed in advance. The directed build IS digest-bound, at sha256:56f440e628ff39e49d92968943c5bce6024503169dfa394671f848f1e98e67e2, and reproduces from his working tree; this schema carries one digest per row and the row's headline is the blind figure, so that value is recorded here in the note rather than in the field.
runs.note: the v0.7 run, and the first run he has posted against a corpus this repository moved to a new predicate version. His own report leads with the blind figure and says the directed one is not evidence about the determinacy of the text, so the blind 179/232 is the headline here: accepts 8/54, rejects 169/176, indeterminate 2/2. The directed pass reached 232/232, accepts 54/54, rejects 176/176, indeterminate 2/2, and is directed twice over in his account -- it followed a spec diff already read and, for bad-902, an adversarial review of his own implementation. He partitions the 53 first-run mismatches by the message the blind build emitted, which he says is the only partition his published run records support: 42 report that aeeRunBinding does not equal the run binding derived from the statement, 7 returned valid with no reason, and 4 report a carried pass_indirect against a recomputed pass. He withdrew an earlier per-fix attribution of 43/5/3/2 rather than restate it, because attributing a recovery to a particular fix needs a bisection against the blind build and that build is unrecoverable. Three rules the directed pass implemented recovered no vector and his blind run never reached them -- the registered networkPosture.posture vocabulary, non-empty signatures, and attribution as a substrate-row validity requirement, forced by bad-823, bad-745 and bad-968 -- so their correctness in this run is directed and says nothing about whether the text determines them; ok-047 and ok-048 are attribution vectors and both were blind mismatches. He claims no reason-parity figure for this run at all: his build emits free prose and no condition codes, two constructions over the same run disagreed at 175/178 and 167/178, and he publishes the ambiguity as a script rather than picking one. The corpus commit he pinned resolves in this repository and carries the 232 vectors of suiteRevision 22.

quotedWording.text: This one is directed, and more so than revision 2 was: the rule was written and the vectors named before this checker ran, so what it demonstrates is that the corrected rule is implementable from the text, not that an independent reader found it.
